sections.body: Segregate defective or questionable products so they are not mixed with accepted products. Status labels, hold locations, quantities, and lot numbers help prevent accidental shipment. Only authorized personnel may decide disposition under the quality system.

sections.body:

Practice scenario: You find a crack in one component, but the adjacent box has not been inspected.
Response: Segregate the component and hold the potentially affected group for inspection according to procedure.

sections.body:

Response: Do not rely on the result; request a tool with valid status and follow the process for evaluating products already measured.

lessons.caution: Do not guess a label from how the contents look or replace a label without traceable records.

checks.explanation: Labels and records link a product to its status, lot, and destination.
options: Maintain product identity and traceability
Replace the quality inspection
Allow a product with no status to be shipped
Reduce the need for recordkeeping

checks.explanation: Resolve uncertain identification before release.
options: Hold the shipment and recheck it against verified records
Choose the label based on the shape of the contents
Replace the label without recording it to finish quickly
Ship it and explain if the customer asks
checks.prompt: Two boxes have each other's labels. What is the safe action?

sections.body: Packaging protects products from damage and contamination during storage and shipment. Under procedure, labels must connect products to their code, lot, quantity, inspection status, and destination. Separating product statuses prevents items from being mixed up.
sections.title: Concepts and Limits of Application

sections.body:
Verify product identity before packaging, use the specified materials and method, and make sure the quantity and label are readable. Separate unreleased items from those ready to ship. Record each transfer.

Practice scenario: The labels on two boxes have been swapped after inspection.
Response: Hold shipment, verify identities using reliable records, correct the labels only under procedure, and document the action.

lessons.caution: Do not leave held products unmarked or remove records to make the area look finished.

checks.explanation: The next worker needs factual information to manage unfinished work.
options: Work status, findings, actions, and the lot or machine identity
Only the next production target
A conclusion without facts or records
Information about a problem after the product has shipped
checks.prompt: A safe handover must communicate…

checks.explanation: A hold status must remain visible, recorded, and handed over.
options: Mark and record the status, then hand the information over to the next worker
Leave the box in the area without notifying anyone
Change the status to passed so the shift can finish
Move the lot to the dispatch line
checks.prompt: A lot is still on hold when the shift ends. What should you do?

checks.explanation: 「引継ぎ」is read ひきつぎ and means “handover.”
options: the staff member in charge
notebook
handover
follow-up message

lessons.response: Record the lot identity, findings, hold location, and person responsible; tell the next staff member directly.
lessons.scenario: Your shift is ending while a particular lot is on hold because of a defect.

sections.body: Shift records communicate product status, quantities, problems, machines on hold, and follow-up work. Objective, timely information helps the next shift protect safety and quality. A verbal handover does not replace required records.
sections.title: Concepts and Limits of Application

sections.body:
Before leaving the area, make sure product and equipment status is clear. Record the lot and machine numbers, facts, temporary action, and who has been informed. Receive instructions for your next task and ask about anything you do not understand.

Practice scenario: Your shift is ending while a particular lot is on hold because of a defect.
Response: Record the lot identity, findings, hold location, and person responsible; tell the next staff member directly.
